text: Three studies. High-resolution sperm typing of the mouse MHC E(beta) gene confirms a localized 1.0–1.6 kb hotspot in the second intron, flanked by recombinationally inert DNA. Crossover rate varies by haplotype while the hotspot stays constant; reciprocal orientations differ, with centres shifted ~400 bp on average, causing biased gene conversion favouring non-initiating haplotype markers—supporting the double-strand break repair model, haplotype s being the most efficient initiator, strikingly similar to human hotspots. CBP and p300 KIX domains interact genetically with c-Myb; the CBP KIX mutation affects platelets, B cells, T cells and red cells only when combined with a p300 KIX mutation, contributing to c-Myb-dependent activation and repression required for hematopoiesis. Tet1 is dispensable for pluripotency; its loss is compatible with embryonic and postnatal development.
